title: Capacitor Array
pages: After the Leaching Vat yields Purified Salts, craft the Capacitor Array with amethyst shards, copper, one lead ingot (forge:ingots/lead), and a salt batch in the center. It charges four Compacted Electrodes into a Charged Capacitor needed by the Flux Rectifier. Build this t3 device before the Electrolyzer.

Build the 10-part bank around the controller: copper block beneath it, redstone block above it, amethyst blocks on the four horizontal sides, and redstone lamps in all four horizontal corners. The lamps are charge cells; any missing lamp prevents formation and charging. The Structure Projector displays the exact layer plan. The lamps may be lit or unlit.

Right-click the formed controller with feedstock from a loaded capacitor_charging recipe. It loads one recipe batch into its stock buffer, processes it over 40 ticks, and holds the output for empty-hand collection or bottom-face extraction. It needs no FE; hand use and the automation buffer below share the same recipes.

It runs 20 exclusive datapack capacitor_charging recipes. Sixteen charge tagged mod ingots into vanilla signal parts: aluminum (2) into four redstone torches, antimony (3) a repeater, bismuth (4) a comparator, chromium (4) an observer, cobalt (3) a daylight detector, gallium (4) a redstone lamp, germanium (3) a target, hafnium (3) a dropper, indium (4) a dispenser, lead (2) two levers, manganese (3) a trapped chest, molybdenum (3) four end rods, osmium (8) a jukebox, platinum (3) a note block, rhenium (12) a lodestone and tungsten (4) a TNT. Three split a nether wart block (nine wart), a quartz block (four quartz) or packed ice (nine ice), which a crafting table cannot do; the last charges four Compacted Electrodes into a Charged Capacitor. With JEI installed, search the Capacitor Array controller for the Capacitor Charging category; it shows every loaded recipe, exact batch counts and formation requirements.

A Charged Capacitor replaces the Resonance Infuser's bottom-right plain sealed steel plate corner, alongside the Wound Coil, the conductive crystal, one vitrified amethyst, a Resonant Rune, the harmonic lens and an electrolyzer. This is the third required t4 apparatus; a plain plate in that corner no longer completes the craft. The Magnetizer later claims the remaining top-right plate with a Magnetized Core, leaving only the bottom-left corner plain.

Automation: the controller also keeps a one-stack stock buffer and a one-stack product buffer. Hoppers, droppers and sided item pipes insert from the top and the four sides; only items that match a loaded capacitor charging recipe are accepted, and simulated inserts never change the buffer. While the structure is formed and owned, it runs one batch every 40 ticks (2 seconds) without power, using the same recipe priority as hand use (lowest resource ID first). Products wait in the buffer and are pulled from the bottom face, e.g. by a hopper under a Stock Hatch that replaces the base part. If the structure breaks, work pauses and progress resets; if the product buffer is full or holds a different item, work waits. Sneak-use with an empty hand on a face to cycle it between In, Out and Off; right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered products. Buffers, progress and face settings are saved with the chunk, and breaking the controller drops both buffers.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer.
